name: ChatGPT: Read (API)
summary: Read a ChatGPT chat via backend JSON and optionally capture every user upload and assistant sandbox artifact in the thread into one zip.
description: Read a ChatGPT conversation by id via the same backend JSON the web app fetches. One workflow with three modes: `latest` returns just the most recent user→assistant exchange (and any planning turns), `transcript` returns user/assistant turns as clean markdown, `full` returns every node in the mapping with raw parts and metadata. Authenticated via the page session — no DOM scraping, no CDP. With `download_attachments` it also captures every file in the thread: user uploads plus every assistant sandbox artifact, wherever it sits in the conversation, delivered as one zip in the browser Downloads folder.

chat_id.description: ChatGPT conversation id (the part after /c/ in the URL).

chat_url.description: Exact stored ChatGPT conversation URL. Open this URL directly; do not start at chatgpt.com first.

download_attachments.description: If true, resolve and download every file in the conversation — user uploads plus every assistant sandbox artifact linked anywhere in the thread (cards and inline links alike) — bundled into ONE zip (chatgpt-attachments-<chat_id>.zip) in the browser Downloads folder. Avoids Chrome's multi-download gate. Enumeration is API-based, so files buried mid-thread are captured without scrolling. Defaults to true.

include_system.description: Only meaningful when mode=transcript. If true, include system/tool turns in the messages array. Defaults to false.

mode.description: What to return. `latest` = just the last user message + every assistant turn after it (final reply + any planning turns) + a streaming flag. `transcript` (default) = user/assistant turns as clean markdown. `full` = every node in the mapping with raw parts, metadata, and parent/child refs.

after_message_id.description: Optional submitted user-message boundary. Returns active-chain reply state in the standard read envelope: not_started, streaming, completed, or cancelled. A later active-chain user turn fails with BOUNDARY_SUPERSEDED.

steps.name: Open ChatGPT to inherit the authenticated session
Allow the SPA shell + cookies to settle

help.summary: Read a ChatGPT chat (latest reply, full transcript, or full mapping with metadata) via the backend-api JSON. One workflow with a `mode` flag. With download_attachments it also captures every file in the thread — user uploads and assistant sandbox artifacts, wherever they appear — as one zip.

parameters.chat_id: ChatGPT conversation id (the part after /c/ in the URL).
parameters.chat_url: Exact stored ChatGPT conversation URL; opened directly, including Project routes.
parameters.download_attachments: If true, download every file attachment — both user uploads and assistant-generated sandbox outputs (code-interpreter patches/zips) — bundled into ONE zip (chatgpt-attachments-<chat_id>.zip) in the browser Downloads folder. Avoids Chrome's multi-download gate. Defaults to true.
parameters.include_system: Only meaningful when mode=transcript. If true, include system/tool turns in the messages array. Defaults to false.
parameters.mode: What to return. `latest` = just the last user message + every assistant turn after it (final reply + any planning turns) + a streaming flag. `transcript` (default) = user/assistant turns as clean markdown. `full` = every node in the mapping with raw parts, metadata, and parent/child refs.
parameters.after_message_id: Optional submitted user-message boundary. Returns the standard read envelope plus response_state; a later active-chain user turn fails with BOUNDARY_SUPERSEDED.

examples.description: Default — clean markdown transcript with attachments downloaded.
Poll the active reply after a sent user-message boundary.
Complete mapping including system/tool turns + per-message metadata.

returns: { chat_id, title, model_slug, create_time, update_time, mode, url, raw_mapping_size, message_count, user_turn_count, assistant_turn_count, system_turn_count, tool_turn_count, streaming_in_progress, messages: [Message], attachments_downloaded: [Attachment], attachment_urls: [...], attachments_zip, attachments_error }. Each Message has {id, role, create_time, content_type, model_slug, text, attachments}. In `mode=full` each Message additionally has {parent_id, children_ids, parts_raw, metadata}. Each Attachment has {source: 'upload'|'sandbox', name, status: 'resolved'|'failed'|'skipped', ...} — sandbox entries add {sandbox_path, message_id, file_id}, upload entries add {file_id, size_bytes, mime_type}. `attachments_zip` is {file_name, file_count, size_bytes, errors}. Envelope shape is identical across modes — only the contents of `messages` and the per-mode count fields differ.
notes: Uses /api/auth/session to read the page session token, then /backend-api/conversation/{chat_id} for the conversation JSON.

`mode=latest` returns the slice from the most recent user turn to the end of the conversation (so callers see the final assistant reply plus any planning/thinking turns that came before it). The final reply is always `messages[messages.length - 1]` when role=assistant.

With `after_message_id`, the read follows only `current_node` and its parent chain without attachment downloads. It preserves the normal envelope and adds `response_state`; only a terminal completed answer gets `selected_message_id`, while cancellation includes `response_terminal_reason: reasoning_cancelled`.
`streaming_in_progress` is true when the latest assistant turn has not finalized (`end_turn !== true`). Re-run with mode=latest after a short delay if needed.

Attachments are enumerated from the conversation JSON, not from the rendered page: every `sandbox:/mnt/data/...` link in any message resolves through /backend-api/conversation/{chat_id}/interpreter/download, and user uploads resolve through /backend-api/files/{id}/download. Files buried mid-thread are captured without scrolling, and the rendered file-card markup can change without breaking this.

Every resolved file is fetched in the page and bundled into ONE zip (chatgpt-attachments-<chat_id>.zip), which sidesteps Chrome's multi-download gate. Fetch-and-zip runs as its own step (s3) because the extension kills any single page eval at 30s; splitting resolution from downloading keeps large threads inside that ceiling.
`attachments_error` is set when a stage ran out of its time budget; whatever was captured before that still comes back.
Gizmo/project user uploads can return 403 from the file-download API (ChatGPT marks them direct_get_only); assistant-generated files are unaffected.
Image generation outputs are not auto-downloaded here — use chatgpt_images_download for that.
